description: Congee with Century Egg is a quintessential Chinese breakfast, offering a comforting embrace with its velvety texture and savory depth. This traditional rice porridge features the unique, umami-rich century egg, often paired with tender pork and aromatic ginger, creating a truly satisfying start to the day. It is a nourishing dish that embodies warmth and tradition in every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice
instructions.text: Rinse the jasmine rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. You may soak the rice in water for 30 minutes to 1 hour before cooking to help it break down faster, though this is optional. Drain the soaked rice completely.

instructions.title: Start the Congee Base
instructions.text: In a large pot with a heavy bottom, combine the rinsed rice with 8-10 cups of water or chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over high heat, then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot, leaving a small gap for steam to escape, and simmer gently.

instructions.title: Simmer the Congee
instructions.text: Continue to simmer the congee for at least 30 minutes, or up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking and ensure even cooking. The rice grains should break down and the liquid should thicken into a creamy, porridge-like consistency. If it becomes too thick, add a little more hot water or broth.

instructions.title: Prepare and Add Ingredients
instructions.text: While the congee simmers, peel and dice the century eggs. Finely shred or dice the lean pork. Peel and julienne the fresh ginger. Once the congee reaches the desired consistency, add the diced century eggs, shredded pork, and most of the julienned ginger to the pot. Stir well to combine.

instructions.title: Season and Finish
instructions.text: Cook for another 5-10 minutes, or until the pork is fully cooked through and the flavors have melded. Season the congee generously with salt and white pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot congee into individual serving bowls. Garnish each bowl with sliced green onions and the remaining fresh julienned ginger. Drizzle with a touch of sesame oil. Serve immediately, optionally with a dash of soy sauce on the side.

tips: For extra creamy congee, freeze the rinsed rice for a few hours or overnight before cooking. The freezing process breaks down the rice grains, allowing them to soften and achieve a silkier texture faster.
Do not skip the ginger! Its pungent warmth beautifully complements the unique flavor of the century egg and adds a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the congee.
Congee can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When reheating, you may need to add a little water or broth to loosen it up to the desired consistency.
